data.narrative:
Strand Therapeutics is a Series B biotech company founded by Jake Becraft, Tasuku Kitada, and Ron Weiss, having raised $205M to date. Valuation analysis triangulates across a universe of 3 public comparables (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers in Biotech & Health, including same-stage and adjacent-stage companies such as Eikon Therapeutics ($539M, Series B), Chai Discovery ($3.8B, Series C), Colossal Biosciences ($10.3B, Series C), and New Limit ($3.1B, Series C).

Two methods prove applicable. Stage-progression anchors to the $205M raised proxy and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, implying $390M valuation. Peer-median methodology uses the median valuation across the four-company sample—$3.5B—reflecting the spread of $539M to $10.3B. Public-comp anchoring is inapplicable due to absence of revenue disclosure. These two methods triangulate to a low of $331M, median of $1.9B, and high of $4.0B.

The wide range reflects material uncertainty around comparable selection: peer valuations span nearly an order of magnitude, and stage heterogeneity (mixing Series B and Series C) introduces timing and maturity variance. The median estimate of $1.9B sits substantially above stage-progression output, suggesting market pricing for frontier-biotech de-risks faster than early-stage multiples imply. Revenue and clinical-stage specificity would narrow this band materially.
